name: Gerbera

cost.display: ~$10,000 (Wikipedia); $5,000-100,000 range cited in user-supplied catalog depending on configuration

characteristics: Strength: Cheap enough to be expended purely as a radar/interceptor decoy, saturating air defense attention and ammunition even when unarmed
Limitation: As an armed variant its warhead is small (<7kg) compared to Shahed-136/Geran-2's 50-90kg
Estimated quantity available: Mass produced; exact fleet size not disclosed
employment_notes: Deliberately flown in mixed swarms alongside Shahed/Geran-2 and Italmas drones so defenders cannot easily distinguish real threats from decoys - a direct, deliberate exploitation of the cost-asymmetry dynamic
contrast_vs_traditional: Gerbera is explicitly built to be mistaken for a Shahed on radar and burn through interceptor stocks meant for the real thing — a decoy doing traditional electronic-warfare deception's job with cheap airframes instead of jamming, which is as much a part of the EW-dependent picture doctrine.md describes as any radio-frequency system on this map.

sources.label: Militarnyi — Russians significantly modernized Shahed and Gerbera drones

notes: Specs meet the bar but the unit cost is an estimate — cost is not verified.
